problem: Existing methods for aerial scene understanding are split into two isolated paradigms: open-vocabulary detection handles category-level semantics but cannot localize multiple targets, while visual grounding handles single-target localization but lacks rich semantic understanding.
approach: OTA-Det unifies both paradigms by reformulating the task to enable joint training across datasets with dense supervision, and introduces dense semantic alignment at multiple granularities to establish correspondence from holistic expressions to individual attributes.
contribution: OTA-Det achieves state-of-the-art performance on six benchmarks spanning both open-vocabulary aerial detection and remote sensing visual grounding while maintaining real-time inference at 34 FPS.

problem: Recent video foundation models produce visually impressive results but suffer from geometric inconsistencies and 3D structural violations, limiting their applicability to world simulation tasks.
approach: World-R1 aligns video generation with 3D constraints through reinforcement learning, using Flow-GRPO to optimize with feedback from pre-trained 3D and vision-language models, plus a periodic decoupled training strategy to balance geometric consistency with scene fluidity.
contribution: The approach significantly enhances 3D consistency in generated videos while preserving visual quality of the foundation model, bridging video generation and scalable world simulation.

problem: Scaling test-time compute via iterative latent state updates shows promise for reasoning, but the internal mechanisms enabling generalization beyond memorized patterns remain unclear.
approach: Equilibrium Reasoners (EqR) hypothesizes that generalizable reasoning arises from learning task-conditioned attractors in a latent dynamical system, and enables scaling along depth (more iterations) and breadth (multiple stochastic trajectories).
contribution: EqR boosts accuracy from 2.6% for feedforward models to over 99% on Sudoku-Extreme by scaling test-time compute up to an equivalent of 40,000 layers, demonstrating tight coupling between performance gains and attractor convergence.

problem: Vlog assessment is highly subjective with no standardized evaluation criteria, datasets, or benchmark, limiting automated systems' ability to evaluate and refine vlog editing plans.
approach: VlogReward defines a comprehensive six-dimensional evaluation framework (Creativity, Consistency, Concept Design, Cinematography, Narration, Pacing), curates a 100k-vlog dataset with VRMBench, and enhances GRPO with adjustable inter-group comparison rewards to address direction blindness.
contribution: VlogReward achieves state-of-the-art results significantly outperforming GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Pro, providing both fine-grained multi-dimensional scores and actionable feedback for iterative refinement.

problem: Discovering task-adaptive communication structures in multi-agent systems remains a significant challenge, as existing methods lack a unified theoretical framework to guide self-organization of agents into efficient teams.
approach: MAGE frames multi-agent graph generation as an energy minimization process inspired by non-equilibrium thermodynamics, using score-based diffusion to navigate the energy landscape via iterative denoising and first-order gradient guidance.
contribution: MAGE achieves state-of-the-art performance on representative benchmarks, and qualitative analysis reveals that generated graphs mirror functional specialization of human organizations, validating the thermodynamic hypothesis.

problem: Extra tokens in Vision Transformers (class, register tokens) lack semantic structure and are underutilized, missing the opportunity to decompose images into semantic parts without explicit supervision.
approach: XTRA augments Vision Transformers with dedicated factor tokens enforced via a novel Minimum Volume Constraint (MVC), plus a multi-stage aggregation process to prevent token collapse and ensure semantically pure components.
contribution: XTRA achieves 8.4× improvement in SEPIN@1 disentanglement over DINOv2 while improving KNN accuracy by 5.8% and linear-probe accuracy by 2.3% on ImageNet-1K.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) lacks convergence guarantees in distributed settings where preference data are fragmented across heterogeneous users, and theoretical behavior remains poorly understood.
approach: Provides the first convergence and time-complexity analysis of DPO in federated and decentralized environments, modeling personalized offline RL with user-specific preference distributions and characterizing the induced global optimization landscape.
contribution: Derives convergence rates quantifying the impact of client drift, communication frequency, and preference heterogeneity for federated DPO, and establishes convergence over general communication graphs for decentralized DPO.

problem: Understanding the loss landscape of high-dimensional neural networks remains fundamentally unclear, especially how local minima are organized and how they relate to gradient-based optimization dynamics.
approach: Studies the population loss landscape of two-layer ReLU networks in a realisable teacher-student setting with Gaussian covariates, showing that local minima admit exact low-dimensional representation in terms of summary statistics.
contribution: Establishes direct link between local minima and one-pass SGD attractive fixed points, revealing hierarchical organization of minima into discrete families and showing how overparameterisation changes their stability under gradient-based dynamics.

problem: Evolutionary multi-tasking accelerates black-box optimization via knowledge transfer but fails in scenarios with many low-similarity tasks due to evaluation budget dispersion and negative transfer.
approach: MES-RET uses a reward-weighted evaluation scheme to combat budget dispersion while employing robust reward-weighted aggregation of mean and covariance statistics to mitigate negative transfer, plus semantic parameter alignment for morphological mismatches.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods on synthetic benchmarks, real-world engineering problems, and RL tasks, enabling skill transfer across morphologically distinct policies.

problem: All-in-one image restoration addressing diverse degradation types struggles to reconstruct content in severely degraded regions, and integrating semantic information into shallow layers disrupts spatial structures causing blurring artifacts.
approach: TPGDiff incorporates degradation priors throughout the diffusion trajectory, structural priors in shallow layers, and semantic priors in deep layers via a distillation-driven semantic extractor and degradation-aware priors for stage-adaptive control.
contribution: Achieves superior performance and generalization across diverse restoration scenarios on both single- and multi-degradation benchmarks.

problem: E-commerce dispute resolution requires grounding pivotal clues from redundant, multi-round, multimodal evidence and making decisions under flexible platform conventions, which existing methods cannot handle.
approach: CyberJurors introduces a multi-agent framework with Individual Verdict Chain-of-Thought decomposing the task into four reasoning stages, and Jury Consensus Verdict simulating multi-round discussion with verdict precedents to mitigate cognitive biases.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art LLMs, MLLMs, and court simulators while achieving stronger alignment with real-world jury voting patterns.

problem: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) enables impressive generalization but safety during adaptation remains unexplored, limiting applicability in real-world deployments where test-time behavior must be safe.
approach: SCARED promotes safe adaptation under the constrained Markov decision process framework, enabling the agent to maximize reward while keeping accumulated cost within a user-specified safety budget during parameter-update-free adaptation.
contribution: Consistently enables safe and robust in-context adaptation across challenging benchmarks, outperforming existing ICRL and safe meta-RL baselines.

problem: Few-shot molecular property prediction faces two challenges: insufficient structural context modeling and redundant auxiliary context learning, leading to inadequate context graph exploration and ineffective information utilization.
approach: ReCoG learns on relational and compact context graphs via a cross-property relational learning module for better structural and relational context modeling, and a context graph information bottleneck module to adaptively suppress irrelevant auxiliary signals.
contribution: Demonstrates the importance of joint relational and compact knowledge extraction in context graphs through theoretical analysis.

problem: Evaluating true inductive generalization of LLMs on entirely unseen data is increasingly challenging as reasoning capabilities expand.
approach: SEDRAS introduces a modular in-context learning evaluation framework with synthetic scenarios varying along three axes: underlying data distribution logic, representation diversity, and interaction dynamics, where models perform in-context scientific discovery and produce interpretable theories.
contribution: Produces 600 diverse evaluation scenarios revealing that different models excel at different tasks, with Gemini 3.0 Pro achieving best overall score but GPT 5.2 strongest on symbolic data, Claude Opus 4.5 on files, and Grok 4.1 when complexity scales.

problem: Applying policy gradients to proactive recommender systems results in deficient gradient estimation due to length-dependent bias and high variance from step-level reward weighting.
approach: ProRL proposes Stepwise Reward Centering to subtract expected rewards neutralizing length-dependent bias, and Position-Specific Advantage Estimation leveraging reward decomposition to compute step-dependent baselines reducing gradient variance.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art proactive recommender systems on three real-world datasets.

problem: Existing jailbreak attacks on LLMs rely on disfluent or incoherent prompts which limit success and make detection easy.
approach: SJA decomposes harmful queries into sequences of harmless sub-questions inspired by Spilsbury puzzles, and employs hyperbolic Hamiltonian dynamics to generate sub-questions capturing structural and temporal dependencies, with hyperbolic narrative fusion for stealth.
contribution: Provides theoretical analysis of how sub-questions evolve along trajectories and demonstrates that hyperbolic Hamiltonian systems capture underlying semantic structure while preserving contextual semantics.

problem: Neural posterior estimators (NPE) trained on low-dimensional summaries suffer from distribution misspecification when test observations deviate from the training distribution.
approach: Introduces minimum-distance summaries, a post-hoc robust NPE method that adapts test-time summaries independently via maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) to the summary-conditional predictive distribution.
contribution: Demonstrates substantial robustness gains compared with existing robust SBI methods using efficient random Fourier feature approximations with theoretical guarantees.

problem: Precise prediction of spatiotemporal dynamics is constrained by high computational cost of solvers and sparsity, noise, and irregularity of observational data.
approach: MERLIN lifts dynamics to evolution of learned observation functionals using functional Koopman theory augmented with Mori-Zwanzig formalism for non-Markovian memory terms, employing discretization-invariant function encoders and resolution-free function decoders.
contribution: Enables full-field reconstruction at arbitrary resolutions and stable long-horizon rollouts even in ultra-low-dimensional latent spaces through interpretable, low-dimensional modeling.

problem: Adapting Detection Transformers to incremental object detection is destabilized by set-based optimization in sequential learning, causing performance degradation through gradient dilution.
approach: FAS identifies three coupled factors causing gradient dilution (signal dispersion, assignment drift, support attrition) and proposes a unified framework with prior-injected queries for focusing, deterministic anchor distillation for alignment, and manifold-support replay for sustaining gradient flow.
contribution: Restores robust optimization throughout incremental learning, counteracting the cascading erosion of preservation gradients in magnitude, direction, and support coverage.

problem: Learning meaningful representations from medical time series is challenging due to high dimensionality, variable length, and noise, and existing self-supervised approaches lack explicit learning of compact, fixed-size, semantically interpretable representations.
approach: Proposes learning k latent Fingerprint Tokens using cross-attention bottleneck trained with dual objectives: reconstruction loss ensuring sufficiency, and Total Coding Rate diversity penalty encouraging disentanglement, framed as a Disentangled Rate-Distortion problem.
contribution: Produces low-dimensional, interpretable, sample-efficient representations where each token captures independent factors of variation, paving the way for more robust digital biomarkers.

problem: While information-theoretic threshold for sparse spiked Wigner model is beta = Omega(sqrt(s)), existing polynomial-time algorithms require beta = Omega(s), yielding a substantial computational-statistical gap.
approach: Proposes column thresholding method attaining Omega(sqrt(s)) scaling under the non-uniformity condition that explicitly rules out uniform spikes, and develops truncated power method for iterative refinement with provable linear convergence.
contribution: Achieves Omega(sqrt(s)) signal strength requirements for both estimation and support recovery under identified non-uniform spike conditions.

problem: Existing decoding strategies are inefficient: sampling-based methods commit to single paths while search methods expend excessive computation regardless of task complexity.
approach: EDEN adaptively allocates computation based on the model's uncertainty by estimating output token distribution entropy and adjusting branching factor monotonically, expanding more candidates in high-entropy regions and following greedier paths in low-entropy regions.
contribution: Consistently improves output quality over existing strategies with better accuracy-expansion trade-offs than fixed-width beam search, with guaranteed improvement over fixed branching within same expansion budget.

problem: High-quality data growth has not kept pace with pretraining needs of frontier models, creating data scarcity bottlenecks.
approach: RePro trains a small 1B-parameter LM with RL to generate effective, faithful rephrasings of pretraining data, optimizing with one quality reward and three faithfulness rewards to maintain core semantics and structure.
contribution: Delivers 3.7%-14.5% relative accuracy gains on downstream tasks by recycling 72B tokens from DCLM-RefinedWeb, improving organic data efficiency by 2-3× while doubling the performance gains of state-of-the-art web recycling.

problem: Current causal abstraction learning methods assume fixed, well-specified exogenous distributions, leaving them vulnerable to environmental shifts and model misspecification.
approach: Introduces the first class of distributionally robust causal abstractions by casting robust learning as a constrained min-max optimization with Wasserstein ambiguity sets.
contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for both empirical and Gaussian environments, enabling principled selection of ambiguity-set radii and establishing quantitative guarantees on worst-case abstraction error, with empirical robustness to environmental shifts and model misspecification.

problem: Existing RL methods for reasoning LLMs rely on outcome-based supervision, leading to inefficient exploration and sparse rewards.
approach: EAPO incorporates multi-turn expert interactions during training, incentivizing the policy to adaptively determine when and how to consult experts, yielding richer reward signals and more reliable reasoning trajectories that internalize expert knowledge.
contribution: Averages a 5-point gain over self-exploration RL on AIME 2024/2025 and AIMO 2025 benchmarks, generalizing to non-math benchmarks including HumanEval, GPQA, MMLU, and HotpotQA.

problem: Streaming tuning strategies for long video generation employ a short-context teacher supervising a long-context student, creating a student-teacher mismatch that caps the student's context length ability.
approach: Context Forcing trains long-context student via long-context teacher, and introduces a Slow-Fast Memory architecture that transforms linearly growing context into a compact representation, significantly reducing visual redundancy.
contribution: Enables effective context lengths exceeding 20 seconds, 6-10× longer than state-of-the-art methods like LongLive and Infinite-RoPE, preserving superior consistency across long durations.

problem: Existing neural network architectures fix topology at sparse or dense extremes, limiting structural flexibility and analysis capabilities.
approach: Proposes Kronecker Generative Networks (KGNs), an algebraic framework constructing topologies via recursive generation rules treating topology as a first-class design object, enabling systematic interpolation between sparse and dense connectivity.
contribution: Demonstrates favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across multiple domains, with KGN instantiations like FractalNet and DenseNet arising as specific cases of the general generation rules.

problem: Benchmark saturation creates dissonance between high benchmark scores and real-world brittleness in multimodal models.
approach: PerceptionRubrics pairs 1,038 information-dense images with 12,000+ instance-specific rubrics derived from golden captions via Circular Peer-Review consensus, using Must-Right (essential facts) and Easy-Wrong (fine-grained details) categories with a Gated Scoring mechanism implementing sharp binary penalties.
contribution: Reveals persistent 5% perception deficit between open-source and proprietary models, demonstrates fragmented element verification despite poor conjunctive constraint satisfaction, and achieves better human alignment than conventional benchmarks.

problem: Ensembles of neural networks outperform individual models but incur large computational costs, while weight aggregation produces cheaper yet less accurate models.
approach: Introduces partial fusion interpolating between ensembles and weight aggregation via neuron-level similarity matching using partial optimal transport, viewing weight aggregation and partial fusion as generalized pruning where neurons can be deleted or linearly combined.
contribution: Enables flexible cost-performance trade-offs between computational efficiency and accuracy, with generalized pruning on single networks yielding similar benefits to partial fusion.

problem: Transformers fail to scale effectively for value functions in RL due to attention score collapse as capacity increases, resulting in learning instability and worse performance.
approach: TQL prevents attention collapse by controlling entropy of attention scores, enabling larger models and effective test-time scaling of value functions through stability-enhancing entropy regularization.
contribution: Yields up to 43% improvement in performance when scaling from smallest to largest network sizes, while prior scaling methods suffered performance degradation.

problem: Explicit reasoning in Vision-Language-Action models incurs non-negligible inference latency and confinement to linguistic space imposes representational bottlenecks failing to capture ineffable physical attributes.
approach: LaST₀ enables efficient reasoning via a Latent Spatio-Temporal Chain-of-Thought capturing fine-grained physical and robotic dynamics, using token-efficient latent space modeling future visual dynamics, 3D structure, and proprioception, with Mixture-of-Transformers design for reasoning and acting experts.
contribution: Improves mean performance across 10 real-world tasks spanning tabletop, mobile, and dexterous manipulation while reducing inference latency.

problem: Universal morphology control for heterogeneous robot policies incurs substantial computational costs and exhibits limited cross-task generalization, necessitating training from scratch for each new task.
approach: DivMorph factorizes randomly initialized Transformer weights via SVD into basic knowledge units, employing dynamic soft gating conditioned on task and morphology embeddings to adaptively modulate units into universal learngenes and morphology/task-specific tailors.
contribution: Achieves 3.3× improvement in cross-task transfer sample efficiency and 16.7× model size reduction for single-agent deployment.

problem: Stochastic gradient-based optimization with categorical variables is challenging due to non-differentiability of categorical sampling.
approach: ReDGE introduces an efficient diffusion-based soft reparameterization method defining a flexible class of gradient estimators that includes Straight-Through as a special case.
contribution: Consistently matches or outperforms existing gradient-based methods across latent variable models and inference-time reward guidance in discrete diffusion models.

problem: Generating high-fidelity 3D geometries under explicit parameter constraints is central to engineering design, yet current methods require large datasets and fail beyond training distribution.
approach: LAMP aligns signed distance function decoders by overfitting each exemplar from shared initialization, generates new designs via parameter-constrained affine mixing in aligned weight space, and proposes linearity-mismatch safety metric detecting when mixed decoders leave valid regime.
contribution: Enables controlled interpolation with as few as 50 samples, safe extrapolation up to 100% beyond training ranges, and performance-guided optimization, outperforming conditional autoencoder and DNI baselines.

problem: Post-hoc controllability of fair machine learning models trades accuracy for fairness significantly, while in-processing methods require expensive retraining for each fairness-accuracy trade-off change.
approach: Proposes learning effective feature representations via gradient-based optimization to improve trade-off efficiency of post-processing fair classifiers, achieving both post-hoc controllability and efficient trade-offs without retraining.
contribution: Achieves trade-off efficiency comparable to or exceeding in-processing methods without requiring any retraining.

problem: Structure-based drug design requires jointly optimizing ligand 3D conformation and binding position, but synchronous diffusion in high-dimensional joint space leads to inefficient exploration and suboptimal quality.
approach: DeCoDe decouples diffusion of binding position and molecular conformation, prioritizing conformation perturbation early and binding position perturbation later, enabling coarse positioning before detailed refinement.
contribution: Achieves 18% average improvement in structural fidelity on CrossDocked2020 benchmark while maintaining competitive binding affinity and molecular properties.

problem: Device-cloud collaboration for LLM deployment requires determining for each query whether to process locally or offload to cloud, but existing routers struggle to judge difficulty from prompts alone.
approach: Enables on-device LLMs to decide internally when to invoke cloud assistance via reinforcement learning post-training with hierarchical rewards encouraging local solving and judicious offloading, plus adaptive prompt filtering to mitigate policy collapse.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines and significantly narrows gap to full cloud LLMs across multiple reasoning benchmarks on on-device-scale models.

problem: While Muon optimizer reduces condition numbers through orthogonalization, the resulting updates exhibit highly non-uniform neuron norms causing certain neurons to dominate optimization.
approach: NorMuon combines orthogonalization with neuron-level adaptive learning rates by maintaining second-moment statistics per neuron and applying row-wise normalization after orthogonalization.
contribution: Consistently outperforms both AdamW and Muon, achieving 21.74% reduction in training steps relative to AdamW and 11.31 percentage-point larger efficiency gain than Muon on 1.1B pretraining.

problem: Natural image generative models assume Euclidean geometry, failing to exploit intrinsic geometric structures within data.
approach: Investigates geometry of natural images and proposes Spherical Optimal Transport Flow Matching (SOT-CFM) using angular distance and Spherical Flow Matching (SFM) constraining dynamics on manifold, modeling images on hypersphere.
contribution: Achieves superior performance against Euclidean baselines by bridging Riemannian manifold-based modeling and natural image generation.

problem: Unsupervised reinforcement learning from internal feedback (RLIF) relies on heuristic intrinsic rewards lacking well-defined theoretical optimization targets and prone to degenerative biases.
approach: PowerFlow reformulates unsupervised fine-tuning as a distribution matching problem using GFlowNet as amortized variational sampler for unnormalized densities, proposing length-aware Trajectory-Balance objective neutralizing length biases and targeting α-power distributions.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing RLIF methods, matching or exceeding supervised GRPO, and enables dual nature elicitation: sharpening for reasoning or flattening for creativity while mitigating over-sharpening in aligned models.
